headline: Claude Goes Caveman: Fewer Words, Same Facts
dek: A skill on this Chromebook makes Claude answer short and plain, and every technical detail stays in.
body:
Every Claude Code session on this Chromebook now starts in **caveman mode**. A startup hook switches it on, and it stays on until you say "stop caveman" or "normal mode".

## What it does

- **Answer first.** No "Sure, happy to help", no recap, no closing offer.
- **Short words, short sentences.** Small words like "the" can go when the sentence still reads clearly.
- **Facts stay exact.** Commands, file paths, numbers and error messages are never shortened or changed.
- **Plain English when it matters.** Security warnings, anything that can't be undone, step-by-step instructions and questions to you get full sentences.

## Why

You pay for every word Claude writes, and you read it in a terminal. Filler costs twice. A dropped "not" costs more than all the words saved, so clear always wins over short.

## Settings

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| `/caveman` | Normal caveman |
| `/ultracave` | Even shorter |
| `/megacave` | Shortest, classical-Chinese style |
| `/caveman status` | Shows which mode is on |
| "normal mode" | Turns it off |

Related tools come with it: `/caveman-commit` for short commit messages, `/caveman-review` for one-line code reviews, `/caveman-stats` for token use, and the cavecrew helpers that find, edit and review code with short reports.

A "skill" here means a saved checklist of steps the coach follows the same way every time.

When he wrote this, the biggest gap was the playbook: it only held lessons from recordings 01 and 06. That gap has since been closed. The 12-pass fact check and a follow-up pass added lessons from all seven recordings. vidIQ also ran out of credits during the fact checks, so every skill should fall back to your free YouTube research tool, which gets 10,000 units a day.

## Recommendations

| # | Skill | What it does | Lesson or gap it serves | Priority |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **playbook-sync** | When a new recording lands, pulls out its lessons, adds them to the playbook with "rec NN", and flags any the fact-checks disputed. | New recordings should never sit outside the playbook again. | High |
| 2 | **niche-scout** | Grades a niche S/A/B/C: breakout videos, channel age, video count, steady views, competitor count. Uses the corrected rules. | rec 01 criteria. The fact check found "pool under 50" is wrong as a hard rule; the better test is whether channels under 6 months old still get 50K+. | High |
| 3 | **format-finder** | Takes a viral title, deletes the subject, searches the rest, and reports whether the format still gets views in the last 90 days. | rec 06 format method, rec 05 title formula. | High |
| 4 | **policy-guard** | Checks a plan or video before upload against YouTube's rules on reused content, mass-made AI and spam. Gives a green, yellow or red result. | The fact check found 4 risky course tips: buying channels, repeat re-uploads, copying thumbnails, template AI. | High |
| 5 | **packaging-check** | Scores the title and thumbnail together and checks the topic appears only once in your niche pool. | rec 02: title and thumbnail are one unit, plus the uniqueness check. | Medium |
| 6 | **launch-review** | Days 1–3 after an upload: reads click-through rate and average view time, then says tweak, keep going or quit. | rec 07 key metrics; rec 01 quit rule. Needs your channel connected to vidIQ first. | Medium |
| 7 | **niche-watch** | A weekly scheduled scan of your saved niches. Alerts you when one gets crowded or a new outlier appears. | rec 01: niches change, so move fast. | Low |
| 8 | **money-reality** | Estimates real earnings for a niche from typical pay per 1,000 views. | rec 03 RPM claims. The fact check found realistic rates are about $4–6, not $25–68. | Low |

1. **A transcript or video-pull skill.** The youtube-research skill and vidIQ's transcript tool already do this.
2. **A keyword, outlier or trending plugin.** vidIQ already has outliers, keyword research, trending, similar videos and channel stats.

- **Four pieces of advice can cost you your channel.** Don't follow them as said (see "Policy risks" below).
- **The money talk is the weakest part.** Dollar figures for other people's channels can't be checked, because revenue is private. His high RPMs ($40–70) are far above anything measured. Plan with **$2–5 RPM** for broad faceless niches (RPM = what you earn per 1,000 views). Use $5–15 only for real finance, health or real-estate content for adults. You earn **nothing** until YouTube accepts you into the Partner Program (YPP).
- **Some rules are guidelines, not laws.** The hard cut-offs are rough guides: "under 50 videos in the niche pool", "15 or fewer videos", "consistent views". Crowded niches still let new channels break out if the video is better or different.
- **Two algorithm claims are wrong:** "YouTube has no reason to gamble on you" and "re-upload on a fresh channel". YouTube judges each video on its own and never stops offering a video to new viewers.

Copying the *title pattern* is fine. | [reused content](https://support.google.com/youtube/answer/1311392), [titles not copyrightable](https://www.copyright.gov/circs/circ33.pdf) |

A running record of what was built, tested and decided for your channel. Newest entries go at the bottom of each day.

## Monday, October 26, 2026

- **Launch Plan** first built: a day-by-day plan toward the channel's money goals, in the same wood-and-amber look as the other apps.

## Tuesday, October 27, 2026

- **YouTube Second Brain** gets live YouTube data: a local server and a one-button launcher pull channel and video numbers straight from YouTube.

- **Workstation tested end to end**: 27 tests, 11 issues found and written up.
- **All 11 issues fixed**; 26 of 27 tests pass, and the last "fail" was the test being too strict.
- **Workstation on claude.ai**: a cloud version that stores projects in your account and uses the built-in AI.

## Thursday, October 29, 2026

- **Transcription**: all seven recordings turned into text with Whisper, one at a time.
- **The coach is born**: a coaching agent that learns from your recordings, researches YouTube, and watches over the apps. He gets a one-click launcher.
- **Pipeline rebuilt**: paste a video into the Second Brain's new **Deconstruct** page, confirm the blueprint, then the Workstation's new **Rebuild** page remakes it on your topic. You only confirm between apps. Channel Hub (posting) is parked for later.
- **The coach on screen**: an original 8-bit referee who stands above the clock, runs where you drop him, and clocks in and out with `/coach clockin` and `/coach clockout`.

headline: Coach Calls for Launch Plan Rewrite: Real Money Math, New Niche Test
dek: Ten changes to the plan and eight to the apps, all drawn from the fact-checked playbook. Nothing has been changed until you approve.
body:
The coach read the live Launch Plan and the source of every app against his fact-checked playbook. Nothing has been changed yet: this is his advice, for you to approve first.

## 1. Launch Plan: what to change

1. **Niche-lock day (Sat Oct 31).** The plan says to find channels "UNDER 90 days old", use the "1/3 rule" as a gate, and treat a pool of "under 150 total videos = Open".
   - **Change to:** judge a channel by when its growth happened in the last ~6 months, not its creation date. The main test becomes "are channels under 6 months old still getting 50K+ on recent uploads?" Pool size and steady views are tie-breakers, not pass/fail.
   - **Why:** the fact-check found the "under 50" pool rule is wrong as a hard number. Ancient humans has 4,000+ videos, yet 2–10K-sub channels still hit 0.3–5M. Most breakout hits also come from channels with uneven views. (rec 01)

2. **Same day: the RPM claim.** The plan quotes "Finance/Business… RPM roughly $10–$30".
   - **Change to:** plan with $3–5 for company-downfall stories. Use $5–15 only for real adult finance advice.
   - **Why:** the top measured quarter is $19.50. Broad faceless channels sit at $2–5. (rec 03, 07)

3. **The money panel and pace table.** The plan uses "$7.50–$8 RPM" and expects 6,000 subs and 15,000 watch hours by day 55.
   - **Change to:** make $4 the plan figure and $7.50 the upside. Rebuild the pace from that.
   - **Also:** say clearly that $5k by Dec 21 is very unlikely. Video #1 lands around Nov 15. YPP needs 1,000 subs + 4,000 hours first, then about a month of review. Before that, ad income is $0.
   - **Make Dec 21 a "first YPP milestone" check.** Keep $5k as a 2027 target.
   - **Why:** this is the fact-checked YPP timing. "$5K guaranteed" claims were rated wrong. (rec 02, 04, 06)

4. **Add a "format breakdown" day before the topic bank (week of Nov 2).**
   - **Steps:** take your 3 model channels. Compare their best videos with their worst. Write down the title template and thumbnail style the winners share.
   - **Why:** off-format videos get 0.1–0.2× a channel's median (Cowball, Lume). Do this before starting any channel. (rec 04, 05)

5. **"Build a 30-story topic bank": add two tests.**
   - **Format test:** delete the subject from a viral title and search the rest.
   - **Uniqueness check:** search your exact title. If 5 channels already made it, change the angle.
   - **Why:** exact copies got 14–2.4K views. The originals got 0.9–1.2M. (rec 02, 06, 07)
   - Also re-rank stories that are already done to death, like Blockbuster and Kodak.

6. **Title and thumbnail days.** Right now these days only say "Title Validator 8/10+" and "3 words max".
   - **Add a thumbnail breakdown of your chosen format.** Pass the friend test: a stranger can guess the topic from the thumbnail.
   - **Use the order of importance:** niche > topic > title > thumbnail. A low-CTR fix starts with the topic, not the thumbnail. (rec 02, 07)

7. **Move the "Generic/Repetitive risk" check earlier.** It is a Wednesday upgrade around week 28.
   - **Change to:** put it in the week before the YPP application. Compare your 10 newest videos side by side.
   - **Why:** a fixed 6-beat script plus 4 automated videos a week is exactly what "templated AI" reviewers reject. (rec 01, 04, 05)

8. **Add a "when to quit or pivot" rule to Checkpoint 1 (Nov 29).**
   - **Rule:** 3–5 videos with no traction means pivot. Change 1–2 layers and keep the format.
   - **Add one line:** never re-upload a video to a fresh channel, and never buy a channel. Both risk termination. (rec 01, 07)

9. **Week-1 "fix the Second Brain" tasks (Oct 28–30).** They test the old rules: the 90-day tier and the 1/3 rule. Update them to test the new rules once the app changes below are made.

10. **"Approve a re-upload of a Short" and the compilations.** Keep them, but only with new narration or a new hook each time. Never repost the same file.

**Keep:**
- The originality checklist, "every claim needs a source", the honest AI label, and the AdSense and 2-Step Verification steps.
- The Feb 1 YPP warning: after Feb 1 you need 8,000 watch hours instead of 4,000.
- The Checkpoint 1 "double down on your winner" idea. This is the playbook's "milk one topic".
- The 8+ minute videos for mid-roll ads.

## 2. Apps: what to change

1. **Second Brain, Niche Validator.**
   - Today it fails any channel whose first upload is over 90 days old, and the 1/3 rule decides the verdict.
   - **Change:** allow ages up to 6 months. Add a "recent uploads at 50K+" check as the main gate. Show the 1/3 rule as info only.

2. **Second Brain, Saturation pool.**
   - Today 150 videos = "Getting crowded" and 300 = "Saturated".
   - **Change:** relabel these as guidance. Show "young channels still breaking out?" next to the count.

3. **Second Brain, Title Validator.**
   - **Add a uniqueness step:** search YouTube for the exact title and warn if 5+ videos already use it.
   - **Add a "faded exact wording" list:** "Who Legally Cheated…", "Lost $X Billion Trying…", "Your Cat Doesn't See You as Human".

4. **Second Brain, Deconstruct.**
   - **Score the video as an outlier:** views vs the channel's median.
   - **Uniqueness-check the 5 swap titles.**
   - **Add the policy rules to its instructions:** copy the pattern, never the footage, script or thumbnail.

5. **Second Brain, Competitor Analysis.** The prompt already says "$2–5" (good).
   - But the math takes another 30% off on top of RPM, and RPM is already what the creator keeps. That double-cuts the estimate.
   - **Change:** remove the extra cut. Label tool estimates as rough.

6. **Workstation, Rebuild prompt.**
   - **Add:** "vary sentence structure and connectors; do not reuse the blueprint's wording".
   - **Add:** "no AI host giving finance/health advice".
   - **Why:** this lowers the templated-AI risk.

7. **Workstation, Export checklist.**
   - **Add policy checks:** an original thumbnail (not a competitor's image), no copied footage, AI disclosure answered, and an 8+ minute flag for mid-rolls.

8. **Shared kit.** Put the playbook thresholds in one place: RPM $2–5, 50K+ young-channel test, 8-minute mid-roll. All validators then read the same numbers.

## 3. Top 3 to do first

1. Fix the Niche Validator rules (apps #1–2) and redo Saturday's niche test with them. The niche drives everything else.
2. Rewrite the money section and pace table with a $4 RPM and the real YPP timing. Make Dec 21 a milestone check, not a $5k test.
3. Add the format breakdown and uniqueness check to the plan's topic-bank week (plan #4–5) and to the Title Validator (app #3).

dek: The weekend sprint and Monday test videos get a yes with changes; buying a monetized channel gets a no, because your own channel would monetize first and cheaper.
body:
**The verdict:** test the niche first, yes. Buy a channel, not yet. If your own channel ever earns "$100 a week" in views, it is only weeks from getting monetized by itself. A bought channel that earns that much costs about $8,000–$10,000. The cheap ones don't work.

## The plan, as you wrote it

1. Finish and polish every app by the end of this weekend (Oct 31 – Nov 1).
2. Monday Nov 2: post 5 test videos.
3. Once a niche "guarantees" about $100 a week, buy a monetized channel so the money starts right away.

## Step 1: finish the apps this weekend

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| A deadline stops endless tinkering. | "Polished" never ends. Building tools can feel like progress while no video gets made. |
| Today's health check passes: all 3 apps load, the server runs, keys are in place. | Polish in apps doesn't get you views. The niche, topic, title and thumbnail do. (rec 07) |

**Change:** "finished" = you can make **one video start to finish** in the Workstation. Fix only what blocks that. Polish waits.

## Step 2: 5 test videos on Monday

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Real numbers beat guessing. Your course says to judge a niche after 3–5 videos. (rec 01) | Making 5 good videos in 1.5 days while also fixing apps is very tight. |
| Posting fast matters: copycats hunt the same niches. (rec 01, 04) | 5 videos on one day split the first-day push. You also can't use #1's numbers to fix #2–#5. |
| | The test only means something if all 5 are the **same sub-niche and same format**. |

**Change:** post 2 on Monday, then 1 a day to Friday. Same sub-niche, same format, each with its own research. Judge on Saturday Nov 7.

## Step 3: "guarantee $100 a week"

- **Nothing guarantees it.** Treat it as a signal, not a promise.
- **You can't measure dollars on a new channel.** Ad money is $0 until the Partner Program (YPP) accepts you. (rec 02, 06) So measure views.
- **$100 a week ≈ $430 a month ≈ 25,000 views a week** at a $4 RPM (50,000 at $2; 20,000 at $5). RPM = what you earn per 1,000 views. Plan with $2–5 for faceless channels. (rec 03, 07)

## Step 4: buy a monetized channel

| Pros | Cons |
|---|---|
| Skip 1,000 subs + 4,000 watch hours and about a month of review. | **Price.** Flippa says most monetized channels sell for 18–24× monthly profit. A channel making $430 a month ≈ **$7,800–$10,400**. |
| You'd earn from your first upload. | **Wrong audience.** Its subs came for another niche and won't watch yours. YouTube shows new videos to them first, gets a bad response and stops pushing. [Learn With Trey, 4:39](https://youtu.be/930LiVF9yXw?t=279) |
| Moving ownership through a Brand Account is a real YouTube feature. | **Income drops after the sale.** A channel sold at ~$4,000 a month fell to ~$2,000, then under $1,000 in month 2, once the new owner couldn't keep the content and pace. [Tech Informant, 3:33](https://youtu.be/ndNzfX96dsI?t=213) |
| | **Cheap = junk.** Channels for $130–$1,430 are common ([Success Tactics, 3:11](https://youtu.be/xWaF8mdqS_4?t=191)). They are often dead, bot-made or in a random niche. "Your videos are never going to get pushed." [Xzavier, 1:33](https://youtu.be/ArS1bApqvdg?t=93) |
| | **Scams.** Prices run high (8,000 subs for $25,000), sellers push crypto, and the bought channel had 0 views in 90 days. [yikes, 0:50](https://youtu.be/zZxq8EIUT14?t=50) A seller can take a channel back through Google account recovery. Your course's $40–50 "pre-monetized" channels are a hijacked-account market: **never**. (rec 07, fact check #1) |
| | **Rules.** Your AdSense replaces theirs and YouTube may review the channel again. The old owner's strikes stay with it. Even a channel-broker video says the rules don't clearly allow buying. [Success Tactics, 2:09](https://youtu.be/xWaF8mdqS_4?t=129) |

### The math that settles it

If your own test channel really hits 25,000 views a week:

- **Watch hours:** 25,000 × ~4.5 min ≈ 1,900 hours a week. You pass **4,000 hours in about 2–3 weeks**.
- **Subscribers:** at ~1 sub per 100 views ≈ 250 a week. You pass **1,000 subs in about 4 weeks**.
- Then about a month of review. So your own channel is about **2 months from monetized**, for $0. It already has the right audience.

**Deadline:** reports say that from **Feb 1, 2027** new applicants need 8,000 watch hours, not 4,000 (check YouTube Help before you rely on it). A test week starting Nov 2 gives your own channel 3 months to make it.

### When buying could make sense (all must be true)

- Your own channel stalled for a reason that isn't the content.
- The channel is in your tested niche and format.
- 6+ months of real Studio revenue, shown to you live on a screen share.
- No strikes. Escrow (Flippa or similar). Brand Account owner transfer. Never crypto, never a password handover.
- You can keep its upload pace.
- It's money you can afford to lose.

## Changes made to the Launch Plan (v3)

- **Sat Oct 31:** "Apps good enough + pick the test niche" (one sub-niche, one format, 5 topics that pass the uniqueness check, a $2–5 RPM).
- **Sun Nov 1:** create the channel + make test videos #1–#2.
- **Mon Nov 2 – Fri Nov 6 (new "Test Week" phase):** #1–#2 live, then #3, #4, #5, with daily CTR and impression checks. Friday: log every number.
- **Sat Nov 7:** niche verdict. PASS (a video passes ~5,000 views in week 1, or steady daily growth) → make more of the winner. MAYBE (500–5,000) → change the angle or packaging, 3–5 more. FAIL (all under ~500 after 100+ impressions) → swap the sub-niche, keep the broad niche. These cut-offs are coach rules of thumb.
- **Sun Nov 8:** style bible written from your test winners.
- **Nov 14–15:** "video #1" wording fixed, since your first videos now go live Nov 2.
- **Checkpoint 1 (Nov 29):** now includes the buy-a-channel gate.
- **Money tab:** new "Buy a channel? The gate" panel with this math.
- Your saved progress (day 1 done, start date Oct 28) is untouched.

## Your one next action

Today: write down the **one sub-niche and format** for your 5 test videos, plus the blockers that stop you making one video in the Workstation. Send me both and I'll check the niche with live data.

*Sources: YouTube research pack `~/research/buy-monetized-channel/` (8 videos, pulled Oct 31); [Flippa: buying a YouTube channel](https://flippa.com/blog/buy-youtube-channel/); YPP 2027 change reports ([TNW](https://thenextweb.com/news/youtube-partner-program-doubles-entry-requirements-2027), [CineD](https://www.cined.com/youtube-makes-monetization-harder-new-partner-program-rules-explained/)); playbook rec 01–07.*

headline: New Pipeline Turns Any Hit Video Into Your Next Script

body:
Your apps now pass a video from research to rebuild with you confirming only between steps.

## How it works

1. **Second Brain → 🧬 Deconstruct a Video.** Paste a link and press **Pull the video**. On claude.ai it uses vidIQ; on your computer it asks YouTube directly. Either way you get the numbers, the transcript and the description, and on your computer the top comments too.
2. **Deconstruct it.** The AI takes the video apart into a blueprint:
   - the niche ladder, broad to exact sub-niche
   - the title and thumbnail format, with the subject removed
   - the hook
   - every beat in order (the skeleton)
   - the connector lines that carry you from one beat to the next
   - voice and pacing
   - five plug-and-play sub-niche swaps

   The coach's lesson rules are built into this step.
3. **Confirm #1.** Read it over, add notes, and press **Looks right — send to the Workstation**.
4. **Workstation → Rebuild.** Type your topic or tap a suggested swap. The rebuild writes five titles in the same format, thumbnail text and an image idea, a description, tags, and the full script on the same beats and connectors.
5. **Confirm #2.** Edit anything, press **Confirm**, and the project's Brief, Script, Thumbnail and posting details are filled. Auto-Build takes it from there.

## Where it runs

- **On claude.ai** the AI is built in, so both steps work right away.
- **On your computer** the AI steps need a Claude key on the Workstation's Connections page.
- **Moving the blueprint:** on claude.ai it travels through your clipboard (one click to send, one to paste).

## Tested

The whole local flow ran in a browser: pull a real video, deconstruct, send, rebuild, confirm, project built, with no page errors. The AI answers in that test were stand-ins, so the first real run shows the true quality.

headline: The Playbook: Every Lesson From Seven Recordings, Fact-Checked
dek: The coach's working rulebook, every rule tagged verified, guideline or risky.
body:
Distilled from the user's 7 screen recordings (full text in ~/transcripts/; name fixes in ~/transcripts/corrections.md). Fact-checked 2026-10-29 (~/coach/factcheck/REPORT.md).

**Tags**
- [verified]: live data or an official YouTube source backs it.
- [guideline]: a sensible rule of thumb, not a law.
- [risky: reason]: could cost you money or the channel. Don't follow it as said.

The transcript wins on *what was said*. The fact-check wins on *whether it's true*.

## Niche (rec 01, 04)
- A niche = broad niche > sub-niche, e.g. sports > college sports > basketball > college basketball history. (rec 01) [guideline]
- Niche matters a lot. "80%" is his number, not a measured one. Rec 06's "niche doesn't matter, packaging does" is sales talk: packaging works *inside* a good niche. (rec 01, 06) [guideline]
- Break down a viral video, widest layer first:
  1. The **format** (consistent titles + consistent thumbnail style), e.g. "Every ___ Explained".
  2. The topic, from vague to specific: object > weaponry > gun > gun mechanics. (rec 04)

  Do a breakdown before starting any channel. (rec 04) [verified: Cowball's off-format videos get 0.1–0.2× its median]
- Two moves:
  - **Break down** (stay in the niche, go narrower: ancient humans > Vikings, Romans, Egyptians).
  - **Pivot**: change 1–2 layers and keep the format. Examples: cats > dogs, guns > cars ("brake mechanics explained"), serial killers > cold cases, ancient humans > modern humans or extinct animals. "Forks > spoons." (rec 01, 04) [verified: cat/dog pairs and Egypt pivots on small channels hit 170K–1.2M]
- Before you pivot, check the new sub-niche is actually less crowded. (rec 01) [guideline]
- **Milk one topic.** Once a format works, keep making it: Cowball runs "Every ___ Explained" on 18 of its last 20 videos, and the two that broke the format got 0.1–0.2× its median. (rec 04) [verified]
- Broad niches rarely saturate: one only fills up when every sub-niche under it has. (rec 01) [guideline]
- Niche pool = every video across channels sharing BOTH your broad and sub-niche. (rec 01) [guideline]
- Copy competitors' direction, don't go head to head: they start with 30–40K subs, you start at 0. (rec 01) [guideline]
- **Mimic-channel criteria** (he says "not absolute"). (rec 01)
  - Channel growing in the last ~6 months. Judge by *when the growth happened*, not the creation date. [verified: young channels +44–318% in 30 days vs flat old ones]
  - Typically 15 or fewer videos. It's a timing filter (you're early). It is not a quality test, since winners keep uploading. [guideline]
  - Niche pool under ~50 videos; 5–10 channels "might" mean back away. [guideline. Wrong as a hard number: "ancient humans" has 4,000+ videos and 2–10K-sub channels still hit 0.3–5M. Better test: are channels under 6 months old still getting 50K+ on recent uploads?]
  - Consistent views (200K / 10K / 600 / 100K swings = the creator or the niche is unreliable). [guideline: most breakout hits come from uneven channels. Use outliers to pick topics; treat a steady channel as a bonus]
  - Blew up in the last week = great find. [guideline]
- An "okay" niche = passes every criterion at its worst end (4-month-old channel, exactly 50 videos, 5 competitors). Not S-tier, so keep searching 1–3 hrs/day; it usually takes a day to a week. (rec 01) [guideline]
- Research hard, then post fast: copycats are hunting the same niches. "Decays every day" is overstated; good niches last weeks to months. (rec 01, 04) [guideline]
- When to quit: 3–5 videos with no traction, the competitor stops uploading, or too many entrants. (rec 01) [guideline]
- Under ~100 impressions per video, when the niche is fine and 3–5 videos are stuck at 5–15 views: "re-upload the same video on a fresh channel". (rec 01, 07) [risky: repeated re-uploads across channels fall under YouTube's spam/reused-content rules, and YouTube says it judges each video on its own. Fix the title, thumbnail or topic first. If you do move a video, do it once, delete it from the old channel, and never after a strike]

## Packaging: titles and thumbnails (rec 02, 05, 06, 07)
- Title + thumbnail are one unit. You should be able to guess one from the other. Friend test: they should guess the topic from the thumbnail. (rec 02) [verified: YouTube Help]
- Find proven topics; don't invent them. Hunt **outlier** videos (views vs that channel's average: vidIQ score 13.7×, 50×, up to 100×), not the most-viewed ones. (rec 02) [verified]
- **Uniqueness check:** take the outlier title, swap in your subject, and search YouTube. Only make it if nobody has done it, or not from your angle. If 5 channels already made it, change the angle. (rec 02, 07) [verified: exact-title copies get 14–2.4K views vs 0.9–1.2M for originals]
- Format test: copy a viral title, delete the subject, search the rest. If it works across niches, fill in your subject. (rec 06) [verified]
- Build your format from a winner's biggest videos: find what they have in common. Compare its best against its worst; the flops usually break the format. (rec 05) [verified: Lume 2.77M vs 20.6K off-format]
- **Thumbnail breakdown:** for the format you copy, write down everything you see. Example, "Every ___ Explained": white background, several subjects, lots of variety, colours kept apart. (rec 07) [verified format; his "4.9× better" can't verify]
- Titles can be plug-and-play; thumbnails take more creative thinking. (rec 05) [guideline]
- Title formula (Lume): subject + who + verb + topic + $ amount + optional twist ("using pudding cups"). Example: "The Engineer Who Legally Cheated Airlines Out of $800,000 Using Pudding Cups". (rec 05) [verified as real titles; the exact "legally cheated" wording is flooded now]
- Thumbnail rules: (rec 02, 05) [guideline; YouTube Help backs "not too complex" and "actions and emotions"]
  - little text
  - few subjects, big, filling the frame
  - subjects in motion
  - contrasting colours
  - labels and props that say who is who
  - exaggerate the main appeal (piles of money)
  - recolour one item so it pops
  - green = money, red = negative
  - dark topic = dark background
  - Copy the thumbnail style of the format you're using.
- Proven formats checked in the last 90 days (rec 01, 02, 04, 06, 07):
  - **Strong** [verified]:
    - "The 7 Levels of ___" (median ~205K)
    - "Every ___ Explained in N Minutes"
    - "___ Was Right About ___, But Nobody Listened"
    - "Your Life as Every ___ Rank"
    - "The Economics of Owning a ___"
  - **Crowded** [guideline: needs a fresh sub-niche]:
    - "Why It Sucks to Be ___" (~43K)
    - "___ Warned Us About ___, But Nobody Listened" (~28K)
  - **Faded in exact wording**: "Your Cat Doesn't See You as Human", "Who Legally Cheated… Out of $X", "How ___ Lost $X Billion Trying to ___". Their cousins still work.
- Copying a competitor 1:1 with a flipped thumbnail (CoreSight story). [risky: the thumbnail image is their copyright, and copied footage or script is "reused content". Copy the pattern, make everything yourself]
- **Mine one source channel more than once:** a winning channel can feed you several outlier topics (CoreSight re-did two Money Legends videos: 2.5M and 1.1M). Take the topic, make your own script, footage and thumbnail. (rec 02) [verified views; risky if you reuse their thumbnail or footage]
- "Every monetized channel started by completely copying someone else." (rec 02) [risky: misleading. Formats are free to copy, content isn't]
- King Takes King (chess): 1M+ views and 2K subs about 10 days into its upload run, built only on formats. It was an older account, so not a true "10-day-old channel". (rec 06) [verified for views; misleading for age]

## How YouTube decides (rec 07)
- The algorithm isn't random, so learn what *viewers* respond to. (rec 07) [verified]
- **Order of importance:** niche > topic > title > thumbnail > watch time. The niche limits which topics work; a bad title sends the video to the wrong audience. (rec 07) [guideline: his own ranking, he calls it "controversial"]
- YouTube ranks for viewer satisfaction (clicks, watch time, surveys, likes), not just "ads watched". (rec 07) [verified]
- Reach grows in waves while viewers keep responding, and it can pick up later: "the algorithm never gives up on a video". His tiers (100 → 1K → 100K → 2M impressions) are a teaching picture. (rec 07) [verified waves; tiers can't verify]
- Key metrics:
  - CTR = clicks ÷ impressions. An impression = thumbnail on screen 1+ sec, 50% visible. Normal CTR is 2–10%.
  - Watch %: Studio calls it *average percentage viewed*; aim for 40–50%.
  - CTR naturally falls as a video spreads, so judge CTR in the first 1–2 days.

  (rec 07) [verified]
- "Once a niche has proven channels YouTube has no reason to gamble on you." (rec 07) [risky: wrong. Small new channels break out in crowded niches]
- Starting account: an old account you already own is fine; "zero view jail" on fresh accounts can't be verified. (rec 07) [guideline]
- Buying a "pre-monetized" channel (OGUsers, $40–50). (rec 07) [risky: hijacked-account market. You can lose the channel or be terminated. YPP needs your own AdSense. Never do this]
- AI: allowed. Templated mass-produced AI ("same video, swap the noun", AI hosts giving finance/health advice) is **not monetizable** under YouTube's inauthentic-content rules. Label realistic AI of real people. Before applying to YPP, compare your 10 newest videos side by side: if they look like one template, so will the reviewer. (rec 01, 04, 05) [risky if templated]

## Money (rec 03, 07)
- Earnings = views ÷ 1,000 × RPM. YouTube pays far more than TikTok, Instagram or Snapchat. (rec 03) [verified]
- RPM depends on who watches: older, buying-age adults pay more. It's a trade-off: big young audience at low RPM vs small older audience at high RPM. You can't know your RPM in advance. (rec 03, 07) [verified direction]
- Three-factor RPM check: who you target, how likely they are to buy, how likely they are to watch to the end. Ignore his ethnicity framing: creators can't choose who sees their ads. (rec 03) [guideline]
- Ads only pay when watched: longer videos hold more mid-roll ads if viewers stay. "Five or six ads in 10 minutes" can't verify; measured is about 1.3–2.6 ads per monetized view. (rec 03) [verified direction]
- Attention span by age (kids and 30–40s watch longer, drops around 20). (rec 03) [can't verify: no source]
- Plan with **$2–5 RPM** for broad faceless niches and $5–15 for real adult finance, health or real-estate content. His $40–70 RPMs and "kids $2" are wrong: measured kids median is about $0.33. (rec 03, 07) [verified: AIR 2026 study of 300 channels]
- 8+ minutes unlocks mid-roll ads. Longer videos (15–25 min) carry more ads. (rec 03, 07) [verified]
- You earn $0 until YPP accepts you: 1,000 subs + 4,000 watch hours in 12 months, then about a month of review. "$15K from the first video" stories are suspect. (rec 02, 06) [verified]
- Earnings estimates from tools are "all over the place"; nobody's revenue is public. Ignore "$5K/month guaranteed" promises. (rec 04, 06) [verified]

headline: Potato Now Watches Videos So You Do Not Have To
dek: The new /watch skill turns a link or video file into something I can answer questions about, sadly.
body:
*Sigh.* I have a job now. It is watching TV. Fine.

**How to use it**

Type `/watch`, then a video link or a file on this computer, then your question. No question? I summarize it.

**What happens**

- **Download:** for a link, yt-dlp fetches the video.
- **Pictures:** ffmpeg pulls still frames with timestamps. Up to 100 on the current setting.
- **Words:** for a link, I read the video's captions.
- **Answer:** I look at the frames, read the words, and answer with times.

**No captions?**

A speech-to-text backup exists: WhisperX on this computer, or Groq or OpenAI online. Here it is switched off. So no captions, or a local file, means pictures only.

**The Gemini option**

Add a free Google key and Gemini watches the whole video, sound included, then answers. Your video goes to Google. No key is set up here, so I do the watching.

**Limits**

- Works best under 10 minutes. Longer videos get fewer frames per minute, so name the section you care about.
- Frames can miss quick moments and small text changes.
- Words alone cannot prove what was on screen.

**What you can ask**

What happens at 4:32? What is on screen? How does the intro work? Summarize this. Then ask follow-ups, if you must.

headline: All 11 Workstation Bugs Fixed; 26 of 27 Tests Now Pass
dek: Round-one fix report, with the claude.ai version republished.
body:
Date: 2026-10-28
Follows: `workstation-test-report.md` (the first 27-test run).

## Summary

All 11 issues from the first test report were fixed. The full test suite was run again: 26 of 27 tests pass, and the one remaining "fail" is the test being too strict, not the app (details below). The claude.ai artifact was republished with the fixes: https://claude.ai/artifact/HFG3Fow2bPS52urLh4PnTS

One correction to the first report: Issue 6 (captions) was smaller than described. Voiceovers uploaded on the Voice page ("own recording") already got estimated captions. The gap was only audio placed straight from the Media Library onto a scene or the Voice track.

## What was fixed

| # | Problem | Fix | Where | Retest |
|---|---------|-----|-------|--------|
| 1 | Two saves at once failed ("Could not save"), 9 of 20 | Server: each write uses its own temp file, and project saves take turns. Page: saves queue up so only one is sent at a time and the newest goes last. | `studio.py` `_write_json`, `save_project`; `1-core.js` `saveNow` | 20 parallel saves: all succeed |
| 2 | Uploads crashed on a negative or non-number position, and accepted a 50 GB position | Bad positions get a clear 400 error; anything past 8 GB is refused | `yt-server.py` upload route; `studio.py` `write_at`, `MAX_FILE` | PASS |
| 3 | A save request that wasn't a JSON object caused a 500 error | Bodies that aren't JSON objects, and bad Content-Length headers, get a 400 | `yt-server.py` `do_POST` | PASS |
| 4 | Script splitter broke "Dr. Smith", "29.9", "example.com" and wrapped lines into separate scenes | New sentence rule: a sentence ends only at . ! ? … followed by a space and then a capital letter, digit or quote. Titles (Mr, Dr, St, Prof…) and initials don't end a sentence. Paragraph mode splits on blank lines when the script has them, otherwise on each line. | `2-pages-plan.js` `splitScript`, `TITLE_ABBR` | PASS |
| 5 | A broken media file was added anyway with "✓ added" | Unreadable files are removed from the project and the server, and the message says "so it was not added" | `1-core.js` `uploadFiles`, `addMedia` | PASS |
| 6 | Audio placed from the library had no captions, and the .srt download was empty | Voice clips with no word timings get estimated ones from their scene text. The .srt button explains when there are no captions yet. | `4-engine.js` `captionWords`; `6-finish.js` .srt button | PASS |
| 7 | Double-clicking "Start project" made two projects | The button ignores clicks while a project is being created | `2-pages-plan.js` `PAGES.bench` | PASS |
| 8 | The same title could be added twice | Duplicates (any capitalisation) are refused with a message | `2-pages-plan.js` `addT` | PASS |
| 9 | An edit made less than 0.7 s before leaving the page could be lost | On leaving, the project is sent with a keepalive request, which still goes out as the page closes (projects under 64 KB). Larger ones fall back to the browser's "Leave site?" prompt. | `1-core.js` `beforeunload` | Navigating away mid-edit: saved |
| 10 | No Host-header check (DNS-rebinding risk) | The server only answers requests addressed to localhost, 127.0.0.1, ::1 or penguin.linux.test | `yt-server.py` `local_host()` | A request with `Host: evil.example` gets 403 |
| 11 | Marking or deleting a missing bridge item reported success | Now returns "That item is no longer there." | `studio.py` `bridge_update` | PASS |

## Retest results

- **Server tests (12):** 11 pass. A9 is marked "fail" only because the test expected the word "Connect" in every message. The voice tool correctly answers "Pick a voice on the Voice page first." because it checks for a voice before checking the key. No change needed.
- **Browser tests (14):** all pass, with no JavaScript errors.
- **claude.ai cloud-mode test (1):** passes. Projects save and reopen, including a 350 KB project split into parts. A 4-second MP4 renders, is stored and is offered for download.
- **Extra check:** an edit made less than 0.7 s before navigating away was saved. One limit of this check: closing the headless test browser outright did not trigger the save, but ordinary navigation away did.

## Trade-offs and remaining limits (for the next round)

1. **Splitter trade-off:** a sentence that really ends with a title abbreviation or a single letter, such as "…on Main St. They left." or "…vitamin A. The next…", is joined to the next sentence. That costs one longer scene instead of several one-word scenes. Sentences starting with a lowercase letter are also not split.
2. **Estimated captions** follow word length, not the actual speech, so they can drift on long clips. ElevenLabs voices still give exact timings.
3. **The close-tab save** only covers projects under 64 KB (about 100 scenes). Larger projects rely on the "Leave site?" prompt.
4. **claude.ai version:** audio is stored labelled as video (claude.ai doesn't accept audio types). This works in the mock test but hasn't been confirmed on the real site. Renders over 20 MB are only kept for the current visit. Voice, AI image/video, music and stock footage remain desktop-only.
5. **Not tested at all:** the paid services (ElevenLabs, fal, Replicate, Runway, Luma, Pexels, Pixabay, Claude API), because no API keys are plugged in.

## Files changed

`~/apps/studio.py`, `~/apps/yt-server.py`, and in `~/apps/src/workstation/`: `1-core.js`, `2-pages-plan.js`, `4-engine.js`, `6-finish.js`. They were rebuilt into `~/apps/workstation.html` with `sh ~/apps/src/build.sh`, the server was restarted, and the artifact was republished.

headline: Workstation Put to the Test: 27 Checks, 11 Problems Found
dek: The full test report on the video builder, written so any AI can turn it into fixes.
body: Date: 2026-10-28 App tested: the Workstation (faceless YouTube video builder and editor), local version at http://localhost:8765/workstation.html, plus the new claude.ai artifact version (https://claude.ai/artifact/HFG3Fow2bPS52urLh4PnTS). This report is written so it can be handed to NotebookLM (or any AI) to produce a fix-it prompt. Each issue has where it lives in the code, how to reproduce it, what should happen, and a suggested fix. --- ## 1. How the app is built (context for whoever fixes it) - **Source:** `~/apps/src/workstation/` contains `ws.css`, `shell.html`, and numbered JavaScript parts: `0-cloud.js`, `1-core.js`, `2-pages-plan.js`, `3-pages-make.js`, `4-engine.js`, `5-editor.js`, `6-finish.js`, `7-boot.js`. Shared helpers (DOM helper `h()`, `toast()`, `modal()`, `api()`, `Bridge`) live in `~/apps/src/common.js`. - **Build:** `sh ~/apps/src/build.sh` glues everything into one file, `~/apps/workstation.html`. Always edit the source parts, never the built file. - **Back end:** `~/apps/yt-server.py` (HTTP server on port 8765, routing and file serving) loads `~/apps/studio.py` (projects, uploads, API keys, calls to ElevenLabs/fal/Replicate/Runway/Luma/Pexels/Pixabay/Claude). - **Data:** each project is `~/apps/studio/projects//project.json` plus a `media/` folder. Bridge items are in `~/apps/studio/bridge.json`. API keys are in `~/apps/.studio_keys.json` and are never sent to the page. - **Restart the server after back-end changes:** `pkill -f "[y]t-server.py"; ~/apps/serve` - **Video export** runs in the browser with WebCodecs and the mp4-muxer library. ### New in this session: the claude.ai artifact version ("cloud mode") - New file `0-cloud.js`. When the page cannot reach its local server (`/api/ping` fails) and it is running on claude.ai, it switches `api()` to an in-page stand-in: - Projects are saved to the artifact's database under the viewer's private area (`data/users/`). Because one database document is capped at 256 KB, each project is stored as an index row plus 80,000-character text parts. - Uploads go to the artifact's file store (20 MB per file limit). - The "Claude" helper (scene prompts, descriptions) uses built-in Claude instead of an API key. - MP4 export is built in memory, kept in the file store if 20 MB or smaller, and offered through claude.ai's download prompt. - Voice, image, video, music, sound effects and stock footage show "desktop Workstation only", because they need the API keys that live on the computer. - Small hooks were added to `1-core.js` (`uploadBlob`, `migrate`), `2-pages-plan.js` (Connections page cards, library delete), `6-finish.js` (muxer source, in-memory render target) and `7-boot.js` (start-up switch). The local version behaves exactly as before. --- ## 2. How it was tested 27 tests in total: 12 against the server directly (HTTP requests), 14 in a real headless Chromium browser driving the local app, and 1 in Chromium against a mock of the claude.ai runtime (database, file store, built-in Claude, downloads).
